title: UK Braces for 163,000 Job Losses as Iran War Bites
excerpt: The Item Club forecasts a 0.4% employment decline in 2026, with retail, hospitality, and manufacturing hardest hit by Middle East conflict fallout.
body:
Britain's jobs market faces its starkest test in years. The Item Club, an independent economic forecasting group, published its regional outlook on May 11, warning that the UK will shed 163,000 jobs on a net basis in 2026 — a direct consequence of the ongoing Iran war rattling global energy markets and supply chains.

**What the Report Found:**
The Item Club projects that soaring fuel, energy, and materials costs — compounded by shipping disruptions — will force manufacturing and construction firms to slash headcount first. London stands to lose 25,000 jobs, Birmingham 12,500, and Leeds 9,800, as consumer spending contracts sharply across major cities. The retail and hospitality sectors will absorb the steepest blows, with the lowest-income regions of South Wales and the Humber suffering the most acute pain.

**Why This Matters — And What Is Driving It:**
The Bank of England has already flagged that UK unemployment could reach 5.6% this year in its pessimistic scenario, up from 5.2% currently. This sits on top of a hiring slowdown that predates the conflict: the KPMG and REC UK Report on Jobs recorded 39 consecutive months of falling permanent staff appointments through the end of 2025, driven by rising employer costs and weak business confidence. The Iran war has now amplified those pre-existing vulnerabilities into something harder to reverse.

**What to Watch:**
The Bank of England's next rate decision and any escalation — or de-escalation — in Middle East shipping lanes will determine whether the Item Club's 163,000 figure proves a ceiling or a floor.
